incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'dedicated-us-west-3' p99 request latency > 3.5s for /v1/generate (streaming). 10% streaming stalls observed. Queue depth climbing -> 220. Auto-scale did not finish warmup handshake. Paging oncall.
ryan: on it. ack -> moving to triage. tagging eng-runtime + eng-sre.
jamal: I’m pulling up runtime metrics now. seeing a sudden spike at 15:02 UTC. warmup success rate for new GPUs dropped to 40%.
sophia: can you paste the pool logs? I want to confirm whether agent handshake timeouts or kernel selection errors.
jamal: paste: ```
[15:02:14] pool-alloc: allocate node gpu-x-12 -> accepted
[15:02:18] warmup: kv-cache init timeout after 4.5s
[15:02:22] runtime-handshake: handshake error: stream-init timeout
[15:02:23] request-queue-depth: 220
[15:02:25] p99: 3.8s p95: 1.2s
```
ana: (support) customer-impact: looks like two mid-tier customers experiencing elevated tail latency: AcmePay and FinLedger. CS alerted both. Maria is on customer call.
maria: on call with AcmePay now — they report repeated partial streams and reconnects for streaming chat. They have traffic spike from a batch job. asking ETA for mitigation.
ryan: quick mitigation options: 1) manual hot-add a few warmed GPUs to the pool (fast but warmup handshake still needed) 2) route overflow to hosted-api (falls back to smaller model) 3) shrink concurrency to reduce queue but increases rejection.
jamal: autoscaler logs: ```
[15:01:50] autoscaler: scale request for +6 nodes issued
[15:02:05] provisioner: nodes launched
[15:02:05..15:02:40] nodes initializing -> kernel probe delays -> warmup step failing on ~60% nodes
[15:03:00] autoscaler: considered nodes healthy=1/6 (timeout 120s) -> cancel?
```
sophia: looks like kernel probe delays cause warmup to fail; likely driver level issue with the new image we rolled last night. Did we push runtime-image:v2026.03.13?
jamal: yes. the new build changed transient kernel args for cudnn/attention kernel selection. rolling back might be fastest.
ryan: operational plan: (A) Immediately open manual routing rule to send new requests to hosted fallback for customers flagged as high-risk (AcmePay, FinLedger). (B) Start rollback of runtime-image on a single dedicated node group to validate. (C) Pause autoscaler new node handshake to avoid adding more failing nodes. (D) Throttle batch size on affected pool.
nana: CS: AcmePay accepted immediate fallback to hosted for 15 minutes while you remediate.
maria: FinLedger also wants fallback. sending instructions to prodops.
ryan: jamal/sophia — can you run a targeted rollback on a small node group (1-2 nodes) and confirm warmup completes? If yes, we can roll-forward the fix. If no, we need to revert the image globally.
jamal: running rollback test now. initiating rollback on node-group us-west-3-a.
jamal: ```
[15:06:12] deploy-bot: starting image rollback: runtime-image:v2026.03.12 -> nodes=2
[15:06:45] node us-west-3-a-21: initialize -> warmup OK
[15:07:10] node us-west-3-a-22: initialize -> warmup OK
[15:07:20] p99 on subset dropping to 0.9s
```
sophia: great. that verifies image regression. next step: pause autoscaler adding nodes with v2026.03.13, force new nodes to use v2026.03.12. jamal can you patch provisioner?
jamal: done. provisioning config patched to pin image for new nodes. autoscaler resume allowed but will provision v2026.03.12.
ryan: enact routing fallback for impacted customers now. [commands] ```
# add routing override
redwood route override add --target hosted --customer AcmePay,FinLedger --duration 15m --reason "dedicated p99 spike"
```
deploy-bot: route override applied for AcmePay, FinLedger.
sophia: reducing max_batch_size on dedicated-us-west-3 from 256 -> 96 to reduce queuing. jamal says it's live.
jamal: batch size change applied. observed queue depth dropping from 220 -> 95 over 60s. p99 for pool baseline now ~1.1s. streaming stalls reduced to 2%.
maria: AcmePay reporting streams back to normal. FinLedger also confirming reduced reconnects.
ryan: next: full rollback of runtime-image for all node groups that were using v2026.03.13. Plan follows change windows: we do a rolling restart across pool to avoid mass warmup at once. jamal please coordinate with infra.
jamal: I’ll schedule rolling replace; will target 10% of pool at a time and watch warmup success before continuing. expected completion ~ 40m.
sophia: postmortem action items being tracked: (1) add image compatibility gate on canary nodes (2) autoscaler to respect warmup success ratio before scaling further (3) improve rollback runbook and one-click route fallback (4) add synthetic streaming checks for p99 stalls.
ryan: tagging product-notify and legal? we should notify SRE pager and customers list. maria continue customer comms.
maria: sending customer update: "We temporarily routed your requests to a hosted fallback to restore low-latency streaming while we rolled back a runtime image; expected full service restoration in ~40m. We'll follow up with root cause postmortem"
nana: oncall handoff note: ryan will remain lead for remediation. jamal will own rollback and infra. sophia will own post-incident validation and SLO adjustments. maria/ana owning customer comms.
incident-bot: [RESOLVED?] p99 for dedicated-us-west-3 back within SLO (p99 < 1.2s) at 15:45 UTC. Streaming stalls <1%.
